subject: Scale & activation SLO follow-up: FluxPay latency, throughput, and test plan
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Porter <samuel.porter@fluxpay.com>, Megan Li <megan.li@fluxpay.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Scale & activation SLO follow-up: FluxPay latency, throughput, and test plan

Hi Samuel / Megan —

Great to chat this morning. Quick recap of what we heard and the recommended next steps so we can align the trial: 

Call highlights / FluxPay targets you mentioned:
- Peak concurrent inference sessions: ~200–250 (short spikes up to ~500 for promos)
- Streaming UX: token-level echo with ~<80ms per-token jitter target for user-visible typing UX
- End-to-end P95 generation latency (first-token): target <= 180ms for single-turn requests at nominal size
- Required sustained throughput: ~1.2k tokens/sec average during business hours, burst to ~6k tokens/sec for 3–10 minute windows
- Acceptable soft queueing: short tail queuing up to ~6s for rare spikes (must gracefully degrade UX rather than fail)

From Redwood’s side — what we propose for qualification:
1) Measurement plan (attached): run three staged tests (baseline, 3-minute burst, 10-minute stress) with p50/p95/p99, token/sec, and per-token streaming latency sampled at 100ms granularity.
2) Autoscale & activation targets: aim for steady-state warm pool of 18–24 GPU workers (configurable), scale-up path to cover 95% of expected spike load within 28–35s, and overflow queue with backpressure to allow in-flight sessions to finish.
3) Acceptance criteria: p95 first-token <= 180ms during baseline; during bursts p95 <= 450ms and no >1% token-drop/failure rate. Streaming per-token jitter <= 120ms p95.
4) Data & instrumentation: we’ll need recent traffic trace (1 hour sample around peak), and a small set of representative prompts (we’ll share).
5) Proposed test window: Week of Nov 22 — Redwood runs instrumentation + you run partner traffic generator; shared Slack channel for live triage.

Next steps / who does what: 
- FluxPay: share 1-hour trace + representative prompts (Samuel) — due Nov 10
- Redwood (Laura + Rishi): finalize test harness, share test-plan spreadsheet and runbook (attached) — by Nov 10
- Schedule a 60m dry-run on Nov 18 to validate tooling and metrics dashboard (Aditya to schedule)

Attachments: fluxpay-scale-test-plan.xlsx (test cases, metrics, thresholds), redwood-onramp-runbook.md (run order + rollback triggers)

If that looks good I’ll schedule the dry-run and set up the shared monitoring dashboard.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0187

From: Samuel Porter <samuel.porter@fluxpay.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Megan Li <megan.li@fluxpay.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:40:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Scale & activation SLO follow-up: FluxPay latency, throughput, and test plan

Thanks Aditya — really useful summary. A few clarifications from our ops side: 

- The 200–250 concurrent sessions is our baseline for payment flows; marketing campaigns can push us to ~600 conc briefly (1–3 min). Can Redwood demonstrate a failure mode that degrades UX to a graceful queued state rather than returning errors?
- For streaming per-token latency: our analytics team measures perceived typing lag at the client with a 50ms sampling window. If you can show consistent p95 token emission ~<100ms during steady state that’d be ideal.
- Cost question: are warm pools billed continuously? How do you suggest keeping cost predictable for our finance team?

We can provide a 1-hour trace from our busiest merchant (will scrub sensitive fields) and a set of 20 sample prompts. We’re ok with Nov 22 test window but would prefer dry-run on Nov 19 if possible.

Megan — can you confirm who on your side will run the generator and who will be on call for escalations?

—Sam
Samuel Porter
Head of Platform Engineering, FluxPay
samuel.porter@fluxpay.com | +1 617-555-0142

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Porter <samuel.porter@fluxpay.com>, Megan Li <megan.li@fluxpay.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 10:05:30 -0800
Subject: Re: Scale & activation SLO follow-up: FluxPay latency, throughput, and test plan

Hi Sam — thanks. Quick responses and what we’ll instrument: 

1) Graceful degradation model: Redwood supports an overflow queue + progressive downgrade policy (switch to compact quantized variant + reduce streaming frame-rate) so clients see slower but correct typing instead of errors. We'll document the exact downgrade thresholds in the runbook.

2) Warm pool billing: warm pool is priced as reserved capacity while allocated; we can propose a hybrid model for the pilot where you get a nightly-prewarmed baseline (discounted trial rate) plus capped burst billing. I’ll have finance ops share an estimated cost delta after the initial dry-run metrics.

3) Measurement specifics: for streaming latency we’ll publish per-token emit timestamps (server-side) and compute client-visible jitter. Recommended metric set: tokens/sec, first-token p50/p95/p99, stream-token inter-arrival p95, queue-length, scale-up time to 80% capacity.

4) Test harness: attached spreadsheet has three scenarios: baseline (1h), short promo burst (3m with 10x TPS), extended ramp (10m with 4x TPS). We also included a control to validate KV-cache cold vs warm behavior.

We can shift the dry-run to Nov 19 — we have availability 09:00–13:00 PT. I’ll coordinate with our SRE (Rishi) and engineering to be on-call.

Laura Bennett
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
